A.explanation: This adds only $V_4$ to $V_2$, but the right-hand branch has two resistors in series so both $V_3$ and $V_4$ contribute to the total p.d.

B.explanation: This adds $V_2$ to $V_3+V_4$, but $V_2$ is already equal to the full p.d. across the parallel combination, so it should not be added again.

C.explanation: This mixes a parallel branch reading $V_2$ with a series reading $V_3$, whereas $V_2$ equals the sum of the two series readings $V_3+V_4$.

D.explanation: The two resistors measured by $V_3$ and $V_4$ are in series, and that series combination is in parallel with the resistor measured by $V_2$, so $V_2 = V_3 + V_4$.

hints: Notice which points each voltmeter connects to: $V_1$ is across the cell, $V_2$ is across the middle resistor, while $V_3$ and $V_4$ are across the upper and lower right resistors.
Recall that components connected between the same two nodes are in parallel and have the same p.d., while p.d.s add for components in series along one branch.
Compare the full p.d. across the right-hand branch with $V_2$, then write the series sum $V_3+V_4$ in terms of $V_2$.
walkthrough: Identify the parallel structure: the cell with $V_1$, the middle resistor with $V_2$, and the whole right-hand pair of resistors are all connected between the same top and bottom wires.
State the parallel rule: p.d. is the same across parallel branches, so $V_1 = V_2 =$ p.d. across the right-hand pair.
Focus on the right-hand branch: the $V_3$ resistor and the $V_4$ resistor are connected end to end in series between those top and bottom wires.
State the series loop rule from Kirchhoff's second law: the sum of p.d.s around the series pair equals the p.d. across the pair, so $V_3 + V_4 = V_2$.
Rearrange with all readings positive: $V_3 + V_4 - V_2 = 0$. This is option D.
